title: Recurrent Corrosion at the Aft Lavatory Drain Interface — Request for a Design Solution

ata.title: Waste Disposal — Waste Tank and Drain

abstract: Maintenance provider request for a design change at the aft lavatory drain interface, where residue tracking along the floor pan produces repeat corrosion findings. Assessed and closed without a modification, the existing service instruction being judged adequate.

sections.request: We look after eleven of these aircraft for three different customers and we are finding the same thing on all of them. When we pull the aft lavatory floor pan there is staining running aft along the joint and, underneath it, corrosion in the structure below. It is never deep enough to be a safety issue by the time we catch it, but it is always there, it always costs us a day, and we always have to write it up. The current instruction tells us to clean and re-protect, which we do, and eighteen months later it is back. We are asking for something in the design that stops the residue getting to the structure in the first place, because the cleaning task is not working.
sections.background: Across the eleven aircraft we have opened this area forty-one times in four years. Thirty-four of those visits found staining, and nineteen found corrosion needing treatment. The rate does not vary with operator or with route structure, which is why we believe it is a design characteristic rather than a servicing practice. We have discussed it with two of the three customers, both of whom support the request.
sections.expected_outcome: A sealed interface between the lavatory floor pan and the structure below it, or a drain path that keeps residue away from the joint, such that the area no longer needs opening outside the normal structural inspection programme.

type_data.business_justification: Nineteen corrosion treatments across eleven aircraft in four years, each costing approximately one day of base maintenance downtime.
type_data.closure_note: Closed without conversion. The corrosion depths reported are inside the allowable limits of the published repair scheme, and the existing servicing instruction already requires re-protection at the interval at which the findings occur. The design office position is that the residue path is a servicing practice issue at the drain panel and not a structural design characteristic. The requester was offered a review of the servicing interval instead.
